summary: Elevate your expertise in water supply and sanitation systems design. Our training offers hands-on experience and insights into effective system management.
lede: Water supply and sanitation design training gives engineers, utility planners and WASH professionals a structured way to plan and review infrastructure. It covers demand forecasting, source and treatment selection, hydraulic layouts, sanitation service chains, lifecycle costing, and maintainability. Exercises use worksheets, comparison matrices, schematic layouts and validation checklists to develop and assess design options, with attention to climate resilience and implementation planning.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who contribute to water supply and sanitation infrastructure design, technical review, or project implementation. It suits people who already work in WASH, utilities, consulting, NGOs, or public infrastructure delivery and need stronger design judgement. Water Supply Engineers responsible for source, storage, and network design. Sanitation Engineers handling sewered and non-sewered service layouts. WASH Programme Officers coordinating system concepts and implementation readiness. Utility Planners forecasting demand and service expansion requirements. Environmental Health Specialists reviewing public health protection in design. Infrastructure Project Managers aligning technical design with budgets and timelines. Hydraulic Technicians preparing calculations and network schematics. Water Quality Analysts interpreting source and treatment data. Operations and Maintenance Supervisors advising maintainability requirements. Consultants and design reviewers preparing technical reports and approval packs.
modules: Water Supply and Sanitation Design Foundations
Demand Forecasting and Water Safety Plan Inputs
Sanitation System Planning and Service Chains
prerequisites: You should bring a calculator, a laptop, and basic spreadsheet skills. Familiarity with water supply, sanitation, or WASH project work will help you move quickly through the design exercises, but you do not need advanced hydraulic modelling experience.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
